newsitem.title: UK: TUC says disappointed by UK interest rate hike.
newsitem.headline: TUC says disappointed by UK interest rate hike.

text.p: Britain's Trades Union Congress (TUC), the umbrella group for unions, said on Friday it was disappointed by the Bank of England's decision to raise UK interest rates, as it was unwarranted by economic factors and would hit manufacturing exporters.

"This is a disappointing decision. We don't think the rise in interest rates was needed to meet government inflation, employment and growth objectives," John Monks, the TUC general secretary, said in a statement.

"We are particularly worried about the impact (the rate rise) will have on UK competitiveness and on jobs in the export industry," Monks said, noting there would also be an increase in the cost of mortgages and that would "hit the pockets of home owners".

The new monetary policy committee, which has been put in charge of interest rates by the newly-elected Labour government, raised official rates to 6.5 percent from 6.25 percent after its first meeting.
It was the first time since the central bank was nationalised in 1945 that it had changed interest rates without being instructed by the government.
